flashcards.q: 1a Define: OO design, class, design pattern, use case, inheritance (5)
flashcards.a: OO design: planning a system as interacting objects. Class: blueprint of attributes and methods. Design pattern: reusable solution to a common design problem. Use case: a goal-oriented interaction between actor and system. Inheritance: a subclass acquires attributes/methods of a superclass.

flashcards.q: 1b Four relationships between objects with diagrams (8)
flashcards.a: Association (plain line); aggregation (hollow diamond, weak whole-part); composition (filled diamond, strong whole-part); generalization/inheritance (hollow triangle arrow, is-a). Dependency (dashed arrow) also possible.
Iterative, incremental: analysis (requirements, objects) → design (classes, relationships) → implementation → testing → maintenance, with reuse and feedback between phases (fountain/spiral style).

flashcards.q: 1d(i) Use case diagram for ABC restaurant (5)
flashcards.a: Actors: Chef, Waiter, Customer. Chef: order ingredients, prepare food, wash up. Waiter: take order, prepare bill, take payment. Customer: browse menu, order food, consume, request bill, pay. Draw actors outside a system box with ovals.

Use case Order Food. Actor: Customer. Pre: seated. Main flow: browse menu → place order → waiter records → chef prepares → food served. Alternate: item unavailable. Post: order delivered. Repeat for Prepare Bill and Pay.

flashcards.q: 2a Importance of OOAD vs other methodologies (5)
flashcards.a: Models real-world objects; encapsulation, reuse and inheritance; easier maintenance and change; better fit for large systems than structured methods that separate data and process.
Standard notation to visualise, specify, construct and document models; shared language between stakeholders; covers structure and behaviour diagrams.

flashcards.q: 2c Inheritance and generalization in an E-learning class diagram (10)
flashcards.a: Generalize Student, Instructor, Admin into superclass User (name, email, login()). Generalization pulls common features up; inheritance lets subclasses reuse them and add their own (Student: enroll(); Instructor: createCourse()). Draw hollow triangle arrows to User; link Course, Lesson, Quiz.
Usability: ease of use. Interoperability: works with other systems. Correctness: does what the spec says. Maintainability: ease of fixing/changing. Reusability: components usable in other systems.

flashcards.q: 3b Library system: identification, classification, behaviour modelling (9)
flashcards.a: Identify objects (Book, Member, Librarian, Loan, Fine). Classify into classes with attributes and methods. Model behaviour with state diagrams (Book: available, borrowed, reserved) and sequence diagrams (borrow, return).

flashcards.q: 3c Purpose of sequence, class, activity diagrams (6)
flashcards.a: Sequence: message order between objects over time. Class: static structure and relationships. Activity: workflow of actions, decisions and parallel flows.

flashcards.q: 4a Two motivations for moving from structured to OO (4)
flashcards.a: Growing complexity and maintenance cost of large systems; need for reuse; structured methods separate data from processes; requirements change often.
Identify inputs/outputs and external entities; draw context diagram; decompose into leveled data flow diagrams; define processes and data stores; check balancing.
Functional: how data is transformed (DFDs, what the system does). Dynamic: how objects behave over time (state, sequence diagrams).

flashcards.q: 4d State diagram of child's bank account (7)
flashcards.a: Start → Empty. Empty → InCredit on deposit. InCredit → InCredit on deposit, or withdraw [balance>amount]. InCredit → Empty on withdraw [balance=amount]. Empty → Closed on close [balance=0] → end. No overdrawn state.
Number of instances of one class that can relate to an instance of another (e.g. 1, 0..*, 1..*).
One-to-one (Person 1—1 Passport); one-to-many (Customer 1—0..* Order); many-to-many (Student *—* Course).
Inheritance, encapsulated classes, polymorphism, design patterns, libraries/frameworks and component interfaces let you reuse tested code and models.
S single responsibility; O open for extension, closed for modification; L Liskov substitution; I interface segregation; D dependency inversion. Give flexible, maintainable, testable designs.
